actual_flow: 1. CM._execute_via_sai: sai_pre_execution_gate(mission_id=CM_CYCLE_1_GOAL_008, goal_id=GOAL_008) -> ALLOW (SAI_adapter pre-gate, logs to approval_log.json)
4. CM._consume_via_gateway(run_id=GOAL_008, goal_id=GOAL_008): calls bridge_runner.consume_executor_output -> ACCEPTED (file checksum match) -- logs bridge_consumed to governance/cycle_log
5. CM._consume_via_gateway: calls classify_execution_request(goal_id=GOAL_008) -> ALLOW (risk_classifier internal) -- logs nothing to governance/cycle_log
6. CM sets gateway_decision=ALLOW in result dict, logs cm_consume_result event to cm_cycle_log

phase6_allow_trace.gap: CM-SAI direct path bypasses get_verdict_for_content(), so bridge_gateway_allow is never written to governance/cycle_log. ALLOW is real but logged in cm_cycle_log only (cm_consume_result gw=ALLOW), not in governance/cycle_log as bridge_gateway_allow.

Q2_reproducible.evidence: T47.8 (stub), T47.9 (stub), T47.10 (production) all identical 4-event sequence

Q3_production_goal.evidence: GOAL_008 source=known_gaps, genuinely pending, no prior execution history

Q4_bridge_runner_verdict.detail: bridge_runner.consume_executor_output() DOES execute (logs bridge_consumed). But get_verdict_for_content() does NOT execute - the verdict/ALLOW logging path is bypassed. CM uses classify_execution_request internally.

recommendation: R2 - T47.11: Add bridge_gateway_allow logging to CM._consume_via_gateway path (call get_verdict_for_content or log equivalent event to governance/cycle_log). Then R1: T48 SAI Quality Validation.
